sub_ok: Hermes is reachable. Phones can connect.
sub_herm: Phones see “Hermes isn’t running” until it starts.
sub_hermerr: Hermes did not answer the check. Chats from phones may fail.
sub_stopped: The service is inactive. Phones can’t connect until you start it.
sub_notinst: aristotle-server.service is missing. Run the installer, then reopen this window.
no_listen: No listener while the server is stopped.
mm_body: The server is version {srv}, this app is version {app}. Re-run the installer so both update together. Actions are off until then.
needs_body: Start the server to read paired phones, pairing codes and the terminal switch.
svc_sub: aristotle-server.service, a systemd user unit. It starts at login and keeps running when this window closes.
dis_running: Start is off: the server is already running.
dis_stopped: Stop and Restart are off: the server isn’t running.
dis_mismatch: Actions are off until the server is updated.
dis_notinst: Nothing to control: the service isn’t installed.
dis_other: Start, Stop and Restart are off while the service is {word}.
d_stop_b: Phones disconnect and can’t reconnect until the server starts again.
d_restart_b: Phones disconnect for a moment and reconnect on their own.
logs_sub: Live from the journal: journalctl --user -u aristotle-server
cap_note: This window keeps the last {n} lines; older ones drop off. Full history stays in the journal.
logs_stopped: The server is stopped. The journal ends at the last line above.
pair_sub: Make a code, then scan the QR in the Aristotle app or type the code. The code expires; the countdown shows when.
pair_scan: In the Aristotle app, tap Scan QR.
pair_fp_hint: The phone shows the same 16 groups. Compare them if you typed the code by hand.
pair_expired_b: It expired at {t}. Make a new code to pair.
pair_none_b: The server has no network listener up (LAN and Tailscale are both down), so the phone has nowhere to connect. Connect to Wi-Fi or Tailscale, then try again.
empty_dev_b: A phone appears here after it pairs. Make a pairing code first.
d_revoke_b: The phone is signed out and must pair again. Its remote terminal grant and open terminals end.
t_sub: Lets a granted phone open a shell on this PC.
t_off_d: No phone can open a shell.
t_on_d: Granted phones can open a shell with full access to your account.
t_off_hint: Turning off closes open terminals and ends their processes.
t_grants_empty: No phone holds a grant. Grant one below.
t_grant_all: Every paired phone already has a grant.
t_prob_b: The remote terminal stays off until the file is fixed or removed. The app doesn’t edit it.
d7_warn: A granted phone gets a shell with FULL access to your account: files, SSH keys, Hermes. Revoking the phone later does not undo what was done.
d7_nogrant: No phone holds a grant yet. You grant phones one by one.
sub_noanswer: The service is active but the server did not answer. It may still be starting. Check Logs if this stays.
sub_nocli: The app could not run ~/.local/bin/aristotle-server. Run the installer, then reopen this window.
sub_outside: The server answers, but not as the aristotle-server service, so start, stop and restart may not reach it.
sub_hermunk: This server does not report Hermes. Update it with the installer.
act_failed_b: The command failed. The message from the server is below.
d_toff_b: Open terminals: {n}. Turning off closes them and ends their processes.
